title: Two verbs for every way of going

blocks.text: Lesson text quoted from the Defense Language Institute Russian Basic Course, Grammar Reference Books I (1970) and II (1965), a US Government work in the public domain (https://www.fsi-language-courses.org/russian/courses/dli-russian-basic-course), from the English Wikipedia's article «Russian grammar», section «Verbs of motion» (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_grammar#Verbs_of_motion, CC BY-SA 4.0), and from the English Wiktionary's entries for each verb, named where a table is given (https://en.wiktionary.org/, CC BY-SA 4.0). Exercises: sentences and translations from Tatoeba (https://tatoeba.org/, CC BY 2.0 FR) and sentences from the library's public-domain books; the answer is always the word the sentence has.

Verbs of motion are a distinct class of verbs found in several Slavic languages. Due to the extensive semantic information they contain, Russian verbs of motion pose difficulties for non-native learners at all levels of study. Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. The roots also distinguish between means of conveyance, e.g. by transport or by one's own power, and in transitive verbs, the object or person being transported.
Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_grammar#Verbs_of_motion, CC BY-SA 4.0)

The present tense has two jobs

The present tense of all Russian verbs has a twofold function; it indicates: A. an action in progress ("actual" function); B. a repeated or habitual action ("repeated" function). However each action of going (to go on foot, to ride, to fly) is expressed in Russian by two parallel verbs: one for the function A — being on the way to … — иду, еду, лечу; another for the function B — usually, often, etc. to go to … (the motion to and from is understood) — хожу, езжу, летаю.
DLI, Lesson 22.
How they conjugate
The verb идти means "to go, be going". It refers to going on foot. This verb belongs to the 1st conjugation (characterized by the vowel -ё-, like живу, -ёшь, -ёт …).

The verb ехать refers to going by some means of transportation, i.e. riding, driving: Я еду на поезде. (Я иду пешком.) Я еду в Европу. (Я иду в комнату.) This verb belongs to the 1st (Е) type of conjugation. Note. — The motion of a vehicle is expressed by идёт (not едет) when time-table and regular route are involved: Куда идёт этот автобус? Когда идёт поезд в Сан-Франциско? Notice also: Танк идёт (not едет).
Лететь: this verb belongs to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that т changes into ч in the first person singular.
DLI, Lessons 19–20.

Ходить, ездить: these two verbs belong to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that the consonant д changes into ж in the first person singular (like видеть — вижу — видишь). Летать: this verb belongs to the 1st (Е) type of conjugation.
DLI, Lesson 22.

Where to?

The goal of motion after the verb идти is usually indicated by the preposition в + Acc. The corresponding question is куда: Куда они идут? Они идут в школу. With certain nouns the preposition на (instead of в) is used to indicate goal of motion: Куда вы идёте? — Я иду на вокзал.

The adverbs здесь (here), там (there), дома (at home) indicate location and answer the question где. They are not used after the verb идти. The adverbs сюда (here), туда (there), домой (home) indicate direction and answer the question куда. They are used after the verb идти.

items: Где он был? — Он был здесь, там, дома.
Куда он идёт? — Он идёт сюда, туда, домой.

blocks.text: The expression "to go by …" (means of transportation) is rendered in Russian by на + prepositional case: ехать на поезде (на автобусе, на автомобиле), лететь на самолёте. The corresponding question is на чём? (На чём вы едете?)
DLI, Lessons 19–20.

exercises.q: Гуси ___ (лететь — to fly, one way) буквой "V".
exercises.why: **летят** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **лететь** (to fly, to be flying) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **летать** for many directions. present: я лечу́ · ты лети́шь · он лети́т · мы лети́м · вы лети́те · они летя́т. — Wiktionary, «лететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  «Лететь: this verb belongs to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that т changes into ч in the first person singular.» — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  Compare: «Капитан летит в Вашингтон.» · «Он иногда летает в Вашингтон.» — DLI, Lesson 22. «Птицы летят на юг.» (The birds are flying south.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))
